# Calibration lab: three experiments on the bill-impact corpora

*Generated by `calibration_analysis.py` (seed 20260731); every number recomputed from the raw run records on each invocation. Input files are pinned by sha256 below.*

**Summary for a demo audience.** (1) Letting the model author its own forecast distribution — five elicited quantiles instead of a fixed transform around a point and one interval — changes mean normalized CRPS by +0.002 [-0.016, +0.021] on 18 matched units, and moves 90% coverage from 71/74 to 45/53. (2) Comparing what the model *says* (stated 80% intervals) with what it *does* (spread of its own resampled answers) gives a revealed/stated ratio with median 0.26 across 728 cells — and giving the model the bill text moves stated width (median ratio 1.00, p=0.97) but not revealed spread (median ratio 0.99, p=0.935) on 36 paired units. (3) A one-parameter interval rescaling fitted leave-one-unit-out on resolved first prints (min mean Winkler, never coverage alone) moves 80% coverage from 115/140 to 103/140 and mean normalized Winkler by -0.03 [-0.13, +0.08] at a nCRPS change of -0.004 [-0.009, +0.002] (n=28 units).

Truth = first print. sd_u = population SD of the unit's supplied history levels; nCRPS = per-unit mean CRPS / sd_u, averaged over units. Winkler score at alpha=0.2, normalized by the same sd_u. All CRPS/PIT via the house 201-point scorer (`scoring.py`, pinned against the TypeScript original). Runs files may still be growing (parallel sweeps); the sha256 above pins exactly what was read.

## Experiment 1 — model-authored CDF vs transform-imposed CDF

The production pipeline elicits point + 80% interval and *manufactures* the CDF shape via `interval_anchor_v1` (fixed knots at p10/p50/p90, 1.5-spread linear tails). Here claude-opus-5 (effort=max, corpus B, no bill text — the measured-best base config) states p5/p25/p50/p75/p95 directly; the scoring CDF passes through the model's own five knots with the same 1.5-spread tail convention, 201 points, and is scored by the unmodified house scorer against first prints.

Gate (reject, never repair): 53 scored; 0 non-monotone rejected; 0 parse failures; 0 API errors. Comparison arms: 74 `plain` runs, 67 `quantiles` (p10/p50/p90) runs scored from `runs_instr.jsonl` (same model, same effort, same prompts otherwise).

| arm | n units | n runs | mean nCRPS [95% CI] | median nCRPS | cov50 [Wilson] | cov90 [Wilson] | cov80 [Wilson] | mean pit-dev [CI] |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| model-authored CDF (5 elicited quantiles) | 18 | 53 | 0.206 [0.141, 0.301] | 0.151 | 28/53 = 0.528 [0.397, 0.656] | 45/53 = 0.849 [0.729, 0.921] | 43/53 = 0.811 [0.686, 0.894] | 0.224 [0.184, 0.265] |
| transform CDF: point+80% CI, interval_anchor (`plain`) | 25 | 74 | 0.213 [0.164, 0.276] | 0.187 | 44/74 = 0.595 [0.481, 0.699] | 71/74 = 0.959 [0.887, 0.986] | 64/74 = 0.865 [0.769, 0.925] | 0.212 [0.180, 0.244] |
| transform CDF: elicited p10/p50/p90 -> interval_anchor | 23 | 67 | 0.212 [0.155, 0.285] | 0.154 | 41/67 = 0.612 [0.492, 0.720] | 64/67 = 0.955 [0.876, 0.985] | 51/67 = 0.761 [0.647, 0.847] | 0.215 [0.179, 0.253] |
| context: bakeoff opus no-bill, default effort | 28 | 140 | 0.253 [0.200, 0.318] | 0.234 | 76/140 = 0.543 [0.460, 0.623] | 134/140 = 0.957 [0.910, 0.980] | 115/140 = 0.821 [0.750, 0.876] | 0.234 [0.211, 0.258] |

Coverage is read off each run's own scoring CDF by inversion (central 50%/80%/90%); for interval_anchor CDFs the 80% row equals stated-interval containment (selftest 4). `pit-dev` = mean |PIT-0.5| across runs (0.25 expected under uniform PIT).

Paired matched-unit differences (model CDF minus transform CDF; negative favours the model CDF):

| comparison | matched units | delta mean nCRPS [95% bootstrap CI] |
|---|---:|---|
| model_cdf_q5 vs transform_plain | 18 | 0.002 [-0.016, 0.021] |
| model_cdf_q5 vs transform_p10p90 | 18 | 0.003 [-0.015, 0.022] |
| model_cdf_q5 vs transform_bakeoff_default_effort | 18 | -0.047 [-0.096, 0.006] |

## Experiment 2 — stated vs revealed uncertainty (no new API calls)

Each cell = one (corpus, model, elicitation, context, unit) with 5 reps at temperature 1.0. Revealed SD = sample SD of the point estimates across reps; stated SD = median stated 80% half-width / 1.2816 (Gaussian-equivalent). The ratio revealed/stated is a consistency diagnostic no single human forecast can produce: it compares the uncertainty the model *admits* with the uncertainty it *exhibits* under resampling.

N = 728 cells (504 corpus A, 224 corpus B). Gates — A: 0 unusable reps, 0 outside the [0.1x, 10x last-observed] plausibility band (analyze.py:136), 0 cells <3 usable reps, 0 zero stated width; B: 0 unusable, 0 out-of-band, 0 cells <3 reps.

**(a) Which direction?** Median ratio 0.26 (IQR 0.14-0.48, n=728 cells); 8% of cells have revealed > stated.

**Does the ratio predict miscalibration?** Spearman rho(ratio, mean |PIT-0.5|): all cells rho=0.209 (p=1.3e-08, n=728); corpus A rho=0.215 (p=1.1e-06, n=504); corpus B rho=0.115 (p=0.087, n=224). Cells within a unit share a truth, so the clustering-robust check aggregates to unit level first: rho=0.267 (p=0.096, n=40 units).

## Experiment 3 — LOO-fitted interval recalibration on resolved first prints

One scale factor w widens (w>1) or narrows (w<1) each stated interval about its point. For each held-out unit, w is fitted on the other units by minimizing mean normalized Winkler score (alpha=0.2; proper, so it cannot be gamed by width alone — coverage-only fitting was rejected as reward-hackable), then applied to the held-out unit. Honest by construction: no unit's correction ever saw its own truth.

**opus no-bill (corpus B)** — 28 units, 140 runs (gate: {'kept': 140}). Fitted w across folds: median 0.84 (range 0.82-0.85); boundary hits: 0.

**Cross-corpus, cross-model transfer** (single w = 1.73 fitted on corpus A sonnet no-bill, 12 units / 60 runs; applied to corpus B opus no-bill): mean nCRPS 0.305 [0.253, 0.362], norm. Winkler 2.29 [1.87, 2.77], 80% coverage 133/140 = 0.950 [0.900, 0.976]. 

**Sealed Thesis-ledger leg: checked and skipped.** Recounted from the sealed snapshot (2026-07-30T15:59:48Z): 163 resolved observations in the ledger, but only 11 score-carrying reward rows pair a stored forecast with an outcome — 8 witness-verified agent forecasts, of which 2 carry a normalization scale — and the export rows carry no interval endpoints (`export_carries_interval_endpoints=False`). The other ~150 observations have no stored forecasts against them. A cross-unit interval-scale fit on 2 normalized heterogeneous-unit forecasts would be noise wearing a method's name; the leg is reported as unusable rather than forced.

## Self-tests (negative-tested; run on every invocation)

- `PASS  house CRPS analytic (uniform, y=0.5): crps=0.0833333333 vs 1/12=0.0833333333`
- `PASS  house PIT analytic (uniform, y=0.3): pit=0.3000000000`
- `PASS  quantile-CDF inversion round-trip: max err 0.1048 <= grid cell 0.7500`
- `PASS  non-monotone rejection: build_quantile_cdf raised ValueError`
- `PASS  interval_anchor pins stated interval at .10/.90: inverted (90.000, 115.000) vs stated (90, 115), cell 0.312`
- `PASS  Winkler fit analytic optimum w=2: w=2.0000, boundary=False`
- `PASS  Winkler fit boundary flag fires: w=10.000, boundary=True`
- `PASS  bootstrap zero-variance CI: {'point': 0.0, 'lo': 0.0, 'hi': 0.0, 'n': 12}`
- `PASS  revealed SD of constant reps is 0: sd=0`
